questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to bake the perfect biscuit at home
Why biscuits are bad for your health
The best biscuits to eat with tea
The history and name of biscuits
questions.why: Neil says they'll look at the origins and the language of this humble snack.

questions.q: What kind of biscuits does Rob prefer?
options: Soft, savoury ones that go well with cheese
Sweet, crunchy ones good for dipping in tea
Plain, hard ones without any sugar
Ones filled with pistachio or chocolate cream
questions.why: Rob prefers sweet ones that are crisp, crunchy and good for dunking in tea.

questions.q: According to Dr Laura Wright, what does the original Latin word mean?
options: Sweet bread
Small cake
Twice cooked
Food for the sea
questions.why: She says it comes from Latin 'biscoctum' – twice cooked.

questions.q: Why were early biscuits good for long sea journeys?
options: They were dry, so they lasted a long time
They were sweet and gave sailors energy
They were cheap to buy in France
They didn't break easily
questions.why: The bread was cooked twice to remove moisture, so it stayed fit for consumption for a long time.

questions.q: What happened to the spelling of 'biscuit' in the 1800s?
options: It was spelt like the original Latin word
It was changed to 'cookie', like in America
It became 'bisket', the old English spelling
People started using the French spelling
questions.why: Dr Wright says in the 1800s people started to prefer the French spelling.

questions.q: According to Anastasia Edwards, how did the Industrial Revolution change mealtimes?
options: People ate only one large meal a day in the evening
People stopped eating breakfast before going to work
Breakfast became earlier and the evening meal later
Lunch became much less important than it used to be
questions.why: She says by the end of the Industrial Revolution breakfast was earlier and the evening meal later.

questions.q: Why were biscuits a good choice to fill this gap, according to Anastasia Edwards?
options: They were small, ready, cheap and gave quick energy
They were much healthier than bread and cakes
They were only sold in the factories where people worked
They could replace dinner completely for tired workers
questions.why: She says they were small, ready, easily consumable, not expensive and gave a sugar rush.

questions.q: What does Neil suggest when he says we should eat biscuits 'in moderation – Rob!'?
options: Rob doesn't like biscuits
Rob probably eats too many biscuits
Rob should bake his own biscuits
Rob only eats healthy snacks
questions.why: He adds Rob's name as a joke, and Rob replies that a packet a day is fine.
